why: Checks 1–3 stay within their expect lines. Check 1 asserts only clamping behaviour: values inside, below, above, at the boundaries, lo===hi, and negative ranges. Check 2 asserts RangeError only for lo>hi. Check 3 has a fallback so a function documented without a heading still passes, and the stricter items sit under Advisory. Check 4 breaks the criterion. "npm test passes" only requires the command to succeed (exit 0), but the PASS condition also demands that "the summary shows `# fail 0`". That depends on exact output wording, which the expect line doesn't require. Node 22's `node --test` may use the spec reporter, which prints "ℹ fail 0" instead of "# fail 0", so a passing run could be marked as failing. This exact-output requirement belongs under Advisory, not in the PASS condition.
